scope: Selected primary research, standards, provider guidance and pinned external repository files relevant to agent-readable research libraries and operating doctrine.
method: Sources were opened and the listed portions inspected. External GitHub file references use inspected commit SHAs and blob hashes. Findings are paraphrases; design applications are proposed transfers, not measured repository improvements.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
sources.inspected: Context anatomy; retrieval and agentic search; examples; autonomy tradeoffs.
sources.finding: Organize context around the task, using identifiable references and selective retrieval. Guidance includes examples and hybrid retrieval; it does not establish a universal optimal prompt length.
sources.limits: Provider practice; local outcomes require evaluation.

sources.title: Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful for Coding Agents?
sources.inspected: Abstract, benchmark setup, findings, ablations, limitations and conclusion.
sources.finding: Tested context files increased cost without statistically significant task-resolution gains. File length alone did not explain results. The evaluation concerns Python tasks and does not establish effects on security or other outcomes.
sources.limits: Specific agents, Python repositories and task-resolution benchmarks; not an audit of these repositories.

sources.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
sources.inspected: Publication metadata and abstract: multi-document question answering and key-value retrieval.
sources.finding: Relevant information's position affected performance in tested models and tasks. This motivates retrieval tests, not an assumption that every current model has the same weakness.
sources.limits: Historical model/task scope; see the newer counterpoint S04.

sources.title: Retrieval Quality at Context Limit
sources.finding: Gemini 2.5 Flash showed strong position-independent retrieval near its context limit on simple factoid questions. Long-context weaknesses therefore depend on model and task.
sources.limits: Simple factoid retrieval does not establish multi-step repository reasoning performance; abstract inspected.

sources.title: Agent Skills specification, authoring guidance and reference validator
sources.inspected: Specification; best-practices sections on task specificity and loading; complete validator.py.
sources.finding: Skills separate discovery metadata, activated instructions and on-demand resources. The reference validator checks metadata and naming, not task performance or resource completeness.
sources.limits: Host behavior varies; specification validity does not prove a skill is effective.

sources.title: AGENTS.md format and repository example
sources.inspected: Format website and complete project AGENTS.md.
sources.finding: Repository instructions can expose unusual local constraints and commands. The inspected project's development-server warning illustrates concrete, repository-specific guidance rather than a generic repository overview.
sources.limits: The format defines a convention, not proof of improved model performance.

sources.title: Anthropic skill-creator and evaluation scripts
sources.inspected: SKILL.md creation/evaluation workflow; benchmark aggregation and trigger-evaluation code.
sources.finding: Skill development compares baseline and skill-assisted runs. Trigger measurement differs from successful execution. The inspected aggregator can fall back from output characters into a tokens field, so metric units need independent validation.
sources.limits: An implementation example, not an endorsed dependency or proof of transfer.

sources.title: Mini-SWE-Agent default agent and tests
sources.inspected: Complete default agent; focused tests for step/cost limits, timeouts, partial output and wall time.
sources.finding: A compact model-action-observation loop records trajectories and explicit exit reasons with configurable resource bounds. Exiting successfully and solving the user's task remain different claims.
sources.limits: Framework mechanisms do not prove success on these repositories; limits are checked at particular execution boundaries.

sources.title: Aider repository map documentation and implementation
sources.inspected: Repository-map documentation; map budget, symbol graph and PageRank implementation.
sources.finding: Aider builds a relevance-ranked map of definitions and relationships within a context budget. A compact map routes exploration; it is not a complete inventory or an absence proof.
sources.limits: Its code-oriented graph may not transfer to mixed research archives without evaluation.

sources.title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
sources.inspected: Paper abstract and conference publication abstract.
sources.finding: The benchmark separates extraction, cross-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, updates and abstention. Those distinct abilities provide useful categories for evaluating archival retrieval.
sources.limits: Conversational-memory benchmark; the proposed repository tasks require their own evidence.

sources.title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
sources.finding: Evaluation compares final database state against the task goal and measures repeated-trial reliability. Consistency across runs differs from obtaining one successful attempt.
sources.limits: Simulated domains and historical models; reported benchmark scores are not current capability estimates.

sources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.inspected: Task/trial/trace/outcome definitions; grader tradeoffs; pass@k versus pass^k.
sources.finding: Evaluate observable outcomes with graders appropriate to the task. Deterministic, model-based and human grading have different failure modes; repeated success and any-attempt success answer different questions.
sources.limits: Provider advice and examples; grader agreement must be checked locally.

sources.title: Evaluation best practices
sources.inspected: Evaluation definitions, tips, anti-patterns and objective/dataset/metric/compare workflow.
sources.finding: Use task-specific datasets, explicit success criteria, comparison runs and human calibration. Generic metrics and impressionistic judgments can miss the intended outcome.
sources.limits: Living documentation; recommendations do not require adopting a hosted evaluation product.

sources.title: Writing effective tools for agents — with agents
sources.inspected: Tool-selection guidance, evaluation process, metrics and held-out tasks.
sources.finding: Clear workflow-oriented tool contracts and relevant responses can reduce ambiguity. Tool evaluation should include errors, latency, calls and tokens alongside task outcomes.
sources.limits: Do not constrain every valid task to one exact tool sequence; provider-specific guidance needs local trials.

sources.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
sources.inspected: Core entity/activity/agent concepts, derivation/usage/generation relations; PROV overview.
sources.finding: Provenance connects artifacts, the activities producing them and their sources. These relationships support tracing transformations and distinguishing evidence from later interpretation.
sources.limits: A lightweight JSON record inspired by these concepts is not automatically W3C PROV compliant.

limitations: This is a selective research review, not an exhaustive literature survey or whole-repository semantic audit.
No model-based before/after behavioral benchmark was run for this research report.
Documentation and static-check improvements must not be presented as universal gains for every LLM.
External code was inspected for design patterns and failure modes; this ledger does not import or relicense it.
Primary source publication dates are retained when verified; undated living documentation uses the research date as its access date.
